lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: The website URL looks like a placeholder.
items.because: It can make the resume appear unfinished.

items.says: Ensure the phone number and email are the ones you want recruiters to use.
Make the code link lead directly to relevant, accessible work.
items.because: An empty, private, or unrelated link weakens the resume.

items.says: Consider adding relevant coursework, honors, or a strong academic project.
items.because: They could support the roles you are targeting.

items.says: Clarify what “update speed” measures and what the 60% improvement is compared against.
items.because: The result is otherwise difficult to interpret or validate.

items.says: Explain what the 400 tests covered and how the rig fit into the build process.
items.because: Readers may want to know whether the tests were automated, how long they took, or what failures they caught.

items.says: Explain how the crash logger identified the five failure root causes.
items.because: The connection between the logger and the findings is unclear.

items.says: Explain how sensor data was buffered and written to flash.
items.because: Memory, data loss, and flash wear may constrain the approach.

items.says: Sampling a 5 kHz component at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The sample rate is below the Nyquist rate.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter `volatile` does not by itself fix a race condition.
items.because: It does not make shared access atomic or provide synchronization.

items.says: The 300-robot firmware rewrite overlaps with a Formula Student claim.
items.because: The resume does not establish which role or project owns the work.

items.says: Define how jitter and field motor faults were measured and give the comparison period or baseline.
Consider putting the strongest, most role-relevant Voltline accomplishments first.
items.because: The fleet rewrite may deserve earlier placement once its ownership is resolved.

items.says: Clarify the basis of the test-time reduction and monthly volume.
items.because: It is unclear whether the volume is the line’s total or the volume processed by the automated tests.

items.says: Clarify the sequence and your role in the diagnosis, process change, and reduction in returns.
items.because: The bullet links all three without showing how directly the profile change explains the reduction.

items.says: Substantiate the return-rate baseline and follow-up period.
Explain how drift complaints were counted and over what period.
items.because: The before-and-after figures are hard to compare without a consistent time window.

items.says: Clarify the throughput comparison and whether the increase was sustained in production.
items.because: The large improvement invites questions about bottlenecks, staffing, and measurement conditions.

items.says: Remove the broad “next-generation, innovation-driven” promotional claim.
items.because: It lacks technical evidence and is less persuasive than the measured results.

items.says: Explain how average current was measured and whether the before-and-after readings used the same operating pattern.
items.because: The measurement conditions are needed to assess the reduction.

items.says: Explain the trade-offs from sleeping and batching transmissions.
Make the project link easy to find and confirm the published materials are accessible.
Distinguish what you built from what the school built.
The robot-fleet work appears mismatched with the Formula Student project and work described at Voltline.
items.because: An electric-car project does not naturally align with a robot fleet.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to writing and testing the CAN-bus firmware.
items.because: The passive phrasing obscures what you personally handled.

items.says: Specify what “tested against the motor controller” means.
The 300-robot motor-control firmware claim repeats the Voltline accomplishment.
items.because: Its ownership, project, and timeline are unclear, especially given the Formula Student title and dates.

items.says: Reorganize the “Tools” category.
items.because: It mixes languages, a hardware platform, and test equipment.

items.says: Clarify the basis for listing FPGA.
items.because: Substantive FPGA experience is not supported elsewhere on the resume.

items.says: Make “firmware” more specific and show proficiency or context for the skills.
items.because: “Firmware” is broad, and the list does not show proficiency or context.
